claims.text: Hf20Mo20Ta20Ti20Zr20 processed by vacuum arc melting, solutionizing at 1400°C, and aging at 600–800°C will form a continuous disordered BCC matrix containing discrete nanoscale ordered B2 precipitates.
The B2 precipitates will be enriched in Hf, Ti, and Zr, while the BCC matrix will be enriched in Mo and Ta.
The treated alloy will have a room-temperature yield strength above 1200 MPa, specifically 1200–1400 MPa.
The treated alloy will have a room-temperature compressive fracture strain above 25%, specifically 25–40%.
The proposed alloy will have a density of approximately 10.5–11.0 g/cm³, with a predicted value near 10.8 g/cm³.
The as-cast Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy may possess a coarse continuous B2 matrix or segregated phases and consequently exhibit high strength but brittle behavior.
Solution treatment at 1400°C for 20 minutes will homogenize Hf20Mo20Ta20Ti20Zr20 and produce a single-phase disordered BCC structure.
Aging at 600–800°C for 120 hours will precipitate discrete B2 particles in the solution-treated alloy.
A continuous ordered B2 matrix is inherently brittle because it has limited slip systems.
Replacing the continuous B2 matrix with a continuous disordered BCC matrix restores dislocation mobility and enables substantial plastic deformation.
Discrete B2 precipitates impede dislocation motion and provide precipitation hardening that maintains high yield strength.
Increasing the Ti/Zr content relative to Hf/Mo and avoiding W or high volume fractions of dense phases will mitigate the density of the alloy.
The treated alloy will have a hardness of 450–500 HV.
The treated alloy will exhibit work hardening similar to the inverted microstructure reported in the cited alloy.
The treated alloy will show no cleavage fracture at room temperature.
The as-cast Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr baseline has a yield strength near 2000 MPa and ductility below 5%.
The as-cast Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr baseline has a density near 12.5 g/cm³.
The approach requires a composition that lies in a single-phase BCC or BCC+B2 region at high temperature and permits B2 precipitation during aging.
Retention of a continuous B2 matrix or formation of excessively coarse B2 particles will prevent the desired ductility improvement.
B2 particles larger than 200 nm will cause brittle fracture below 5% strain in the proposed alloy.
